data.title: Singapore accounting body inks AI deal with Indian counterpart
data.description:
The deal could extend ISCA's AI programme to India's 1.5 million accounting professionals.

The Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants (ISCA) has signed a Letter of Cooperation with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) to explore extending its AI Fluency Programme to ICAI's community of more than 1.5 million members and students.

The proposed arrangement, signed on 21 August, centres on ISCA's approximately 30-hour programme comprising 180 hands-on workplace cases. The curriculum covers three areas: foundational AI skills for everyday professional use, AI applications across accounting, audit, finance and tax functions, and AI leadership and governance.

In parallel, ISCA has approved a proposed Module Exemption Agreement (MEA) with ICAI that would provide exemptions under each body's professional qualification pathways. Exemptions under ISCA's Singapore Chartered Accountant Qualification (SCAQ) for eligible ICAI members take effect from 21 August, though formal execution of the MEA remains subject to approvals in India.

"AI is reshaping the accountancy profession and building AI fluency alongside strong professional expertise will be critical to enabling the profession to adapt and create greater value," said Lee Boon Teck, President of ISCA. "Through the proposed Global AI Fluency initiative, we hope to share Singapore's experience in practical and responsible AI capability development with a wider professional community."

Whilst formal execution of the MEA remains subject to approvals in India, ISCA is implementing the specified SCAQ exemptions for eligible ICAI members with effect from 21 August. The AI collaboration remains subject to relevant approvals and mutually agreed implementation arrangements.

data.title: Singapore, India ink MoUs on food safety and maritime heritage
data.description:
Both also signed a telecoms-broadcasting cooperation letter.

Singapore and India have signed two memoranda of understanding covering food safety and maritime heritage cooperation following the fourth India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable on 20 August.

The two countries also exchanged a Letter of Intent between the Infocomm Media Development Authority and the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India covering cooperation in telecommunications and broadcasting.

In addition, both sides discussed cooperation in sustainability, digitalisation, skills development, healthcare and medicine, advanced manufacturing, and connectivity.

Singapore and India agreed to further advance the National Centre of Excellence for Advanced Manufacturing in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, which will be supported by the Singapore Cooperation Programme.

Indian companies also explored ways to use Singapore as a platform to access international markets.

data.title: Domestic wholesale sales up 20.3% in Q2
data.description:
Foreign wholesale sales grew 28.6% YoY.

Domestic wholesale sales rose 20.3% year on year in the second quarter of 2026, according to the Singapore Department of Statistics.

Excluding petroleum, domestic wholesale sales increased 21.4% to about $55b.

On a seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter basis, sales grew 13.5%, or 10% excluding petroleum.

General wholesale trade recorded a 67% year-on-year increase in domestic sales, driven by higher commodity sales volumes and prices. Ship chandlers & bunkering sales rose 56.5% on higher bunker fuel prices.

Metals, timber & construction materials sales fell 23.6% due to lower metals sales volumes.

Meanwhile, foreign wholesale sales rose 28.6% year on year to an estimated $1.191t. Excluding petroleum, foreign sales increased 21.9% to about $663b.

On a seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter basis, foreign wholesale sales grew 16.7%, or 8.4% excluding petroleum.

Electronic Components recorded a 54.4% YoY increase in foreign sales on higher prices and sales volumes. Telecommunications & computers sales rose 39.6% on higher sales volumes of computer hardware and accessories.

Other wholesale trade sales fell 1.6% due to weaker global demand for agricultural products.

data.title: IMDA, SAL and SCCA launch AI training tracks for legal professionals
data.description:
The initiatives will run over the next three years.

The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), Singapore Academy of Law (SAL), and Singapore Corporate Counsel Association (SCCA) have launched two artificial intelligence (AI) training programmes for legal professionals.

The programmes will run over the next three years and were developed under the National AI Impact Programme.

AIxLegal by SAL targets practising lawyers, covering the use of AI in legal research, drafting, and case analysis.

Meanwhile, AIxLegal by SCCA targets in-house counsel and allied legal professionals, with training focused on corporate legal workflows such as contract management, document management, and legal research.

The initiatives build on IMDA’s work with the Ministry of Law, SAL, and SCCA to expand AI use across the legal profession.

Separately, the authority is expanding its TechSkills Accelerator initiative to offer almost 2,000 tech job and training opportunities with more than 20 companies.

The place-and-train opportunities will be available to fresh graduates and mid-career professionals seeking to enter the technology sector.

Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo announced the programmes and the additional job and training opportunities at the Singapore Computer Society Tech3 Forum 2026.

data.title: Kimly sets sights on SGX Mainboard transfer
data.description:
The move would support larger investments and acquisitions.

Kimly Limited plans to transfer its listing from the Catalist Board to the Mainboard of the Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited (SGX-ST), subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.

The company said moving to the Mainboard would broaden its investor base and improve access to capital and potential strategic opportunities.

It also said the move would support its plans to pursue larger-scale investments and acquisitions.

The company has been listed on Catalist since March 20, 2017.

It operates traditional coffee shops and food outlets through three business segments: outlet management, outlet investment, and food retail.

Kimly said it plans to pursue further growth through organic expansion, investments, diversification, and acquisitions.

It is also considering businesses that are adjacent and complementary to its existing operations, including opportunities in the halal market.

The transfer requires, amongst other things, in-principle approval from the SGX-ST, compliance with the listing requirements for a Catalist-to-Mainboard transfer, and shareholder approval through a special resolution at an extraordinary general meeting.

Kimly will prepare and submit its application through its sponsor, PrimePartners Corporate Finance Pte. Ltd.

The company plans to hold the extraordinary general meeting in January 2027, on the same day as its annual general meeting, subject to the relevant arrangements.

A shareholder circular containing details of the proposed transfer and the notice of the extraordinary general meeting will be issued at a later date.

data.title: Gather House exceeds 90% occupancy after soft launch
data.description:
Phase 1 opened in early August with 72 beds for younger independent travellers.

The Assembly Place Holdings Ltd. (TAP) has recorded occupancy of above 90% at Gather House’s 72-bed first phase following the premium capsule hostel’s soft launch in early August.

Located at 63 and 65 South Bridge Road, Gather House is being developed in two phases and will have 132 beds upon completion.

Phase 1 at 65 South Bridge Road comprises 72 beds, whilst Phase 2 at 63 South Bridge Road will add 60 beds and is pending its Temporary Occupation Permit.

Gather House targets younger and independent travellers seeking a balance between affordability, comfort, and experience.

Guests can also access member services and curated experiences through TAP’s network of service providers.

The launch marks TAP’s entry into the premium capsule hostel segment and its eighth brand. It follows the group’s expansion into multiple accommodation segments since its listing on the Singapore Exchange in January 2026.

TAP has entered the migrant workers’ accommodation segment through a joint venture, acquired 163 Tras Street for conversion into a hotel, and secured the lease of Char Yong (Dabu) Building for its artificial intelligence-powered co-living concept.

It also formed a joint venture to transform Phoenix Park into a community living destination and participated in a JV to redevelop a freehold site in Bukit Timah, where TAP is the project manager and is involved in sales and marketing.

data.title: ComfortDelGro’s Zig invests over $10m in EVs, hybrids for hire fleet
data.description:
Vantage Automotive will supply BYD M6 and SEAL 6 models amidst strong hirer demand.

Zig by ComfortDelGro is investing over $10m in its private hire vehicle fleet with new electric and hybrid vehicles supplied by Vantage Automotive.

The fleet will include BYD models such as the fully electric BYD M6 and the BYD SEAL 6 DM-i hybrid.

The group said the vehicles will be progressively added to its private hire fleet and made available to hirers in the coming months.

Hirers will also receive preferential charging rates through CDG Energy, as well as maintenance support from ComfortDelGro Engineering’s automotive workshop network.

The investment comes amidst stronger demand for private hire vehicles (PHV), said Michael Huang, head of Singapore Point-to-Point Mobility Business.

“Investing in our PHV fleet gives hirers more options and strengthens our ability to support mobility demand across Singapore,” Huang added.

data.title: Tuas Power secures 670-MW gas unit
data.description:
The facility is expected to begin commercial operations by December 2031.

Singapore’s Energy Market Authority (EMA) has awarded Tuas Power Generation Pte Ltd (Tuas Power) the right to build, own, and operate a new combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) generating unit, the authority announced on 20 August.

This follows an RFP launched by EMA in April under its centralised process for new generation capacity to ensure sufficient power generation capacity to meet Singapore’s future electricity needs.

Tuas Power’s CCGT is expected to provide 670 megawatts of power generation capacity and be ready for commercial operations by December 2031.

“These CCGTs powered by natural gas will provide reliable baseload power, whilst we pursue diverse pathways to a cleaner energy future,” said Puah Kok Keong, CEO of EMA.

Singapore’s electricity demand is projected to grow by 2.4% to 4.8% annually over the next decade, according to EMA.

By 2031, peak electricity demand is projected to reach between 9.6 gigawatts (GW) and 11.4 GW, the authority said.

Demand will be driven by strong economic growth, transport electrification, and the expansion of energy-intensive sectors such as semiconductor manufacturing and data centres.

The installed capacity could meet the electricity demand of up to about 1.2 million four-room HDB households annually, according to EMA.

data.title: SCS unveils AI skills pathway for specialist, non-tech roles
data.description:
Two tracks cover five entry-level jobs and training for business users. 

The Singapore Computer Society (SCS) has launched a skills pathway for artificial intelligence (AI), covering non-technical professionals and specialist AI roles.

It is divided into two tracks — the AI Bilingual Pathway and the AI Technical Specialist Pathway.

The first track covers baseline knowledge, practical application and governance, aimed at non-tech practitioners, domain professionals, and business users. Participants are recommended to complete at least one course or certification in each of the three areas. 

Meanwhile, the AI Technical Specialist Pathway targets aspiring AI professionals through employer-recognised certifications, portfolio development, and technical assessment guidance.

It covers five entry-level roles —  AI Platform Engineer, AI Application Engineer, AI Solutions Architect, AI Product Manager, and AI Ethics & Compliance Officer.

The AI programme is the third Skills Pathway developed by SCS as a Skills Development Partner, following its cybersecurity pathway in 2024 and cloud pathway in 2025.

The initiative is supported by the Skills & Workforce Development Agency, Infocomm Media Development Authority, AI Singapore, the Singapore Medical Association, Institution of Engineers Singapore, Singapore Logistics Association, and 15 founding employers.
